# Root observations while original English-first reading remains independent

No semantic decision or acceptance. Do not share this file with either original
angle. The reconciliation/semantic roles may read it only after both freeze.

The frozen Tibetan-first files contain 84 spans (33/39/12), no nulls, 64 d5
pairs. Root read all reports, notes and spans, verified 89 frozen files and eight
historical governing Git pins, and checked all saved occurrence slices against
the original spine. Root canonical replay waits for both originals, then runs
all six current bodies; the producer has exit0 on each with failed attempts kept.

- 256: cig car du/together excludes sit down although HGM4169 includes both
  the wide rendering and together; do not say the wider wording is unattested.
  The flat wet/flowing splits and intact chur/bdud rtsir words need comparison
  against any defensible whole phrase/member alternative. Exact source case and
  reality predicates must not be lost through English to-the-eyes-of recasts.
- 257: 'ga' zhig/only one or two of them has exact whole HGM2545 support as
  well as one or two and other variants. Challenge scope while confronting that
  positive record. It cannot be rejected by falsely asserting no such gloss.
  The two deictic/alternative d3 recasts contain supplied-person discourse words;
  check whole construction licensing rather than using d3 to hide a false atom.
  All five tshad ma appearances are separately resolved. The allocation of ma
  'khrul ba versus rtogs par/correctly perceives needs direct local grammar and
  actual HGM evidence. Compare the complete incompatible-ways phrase to the
  proposed 'gal ba/completely incompatible word; the preposition does not itself
  license the English completely. Full lexical records are saved separately.
- 258: both HGM11687 and HGM3657 were reopened: phan tshun spangs 'gal includes
  the entire if-something-exists definition and directly incompatible; dngos
  'gal includes directly incompatible. The Tibetan candidate deliberately
  assigns the definition to the former at d3 and the label to the latter at d5.
  Determine semantic/source ownership independently; agreement with a glossary
  or source-byte fidelity is not by itself approval. The one Tibetan chu has
  two English water mentions; avoid a fabricated second source occurrence.

Original master, source words, variants and all failed attempts stay unchanged.

The supplementary exact query confirms positive evidence: HGM2555 'gal ba
explicitly includes completely incompatible; HGM6760 rtogs pa explicitly includes
correctly perceives. The source-inflected rtogs par has its own narrower exact
entry6787 (have realized/realizes/realized); compare morphological relation and
full variants rather than conflating those two rows. HGM13708 ma 'khrul ba has
unmistaken/valid. These records must be confronted in any scope rejection.

## After both original angles froze

The independent English files have 88 spans (39/36/13), 62 d5 and six d7,
zero nulls/errata. Root read all reports, specs and notes; its 100-file freeze
and eight Git pins pass. All six original canonical bodies now replay exactly
and all 172 original ranges resolve. These are fidelity proofs, not acceptance.

The actual English master evidence has the base compound thad ka thad ka with
HGM different type; the source has the inflected thad ka thad kar. Do not
confuse this compound with thad ka/radius, but verify morphology and actual
role before retaining English's mapping. Its four ngo bor/to-the-perceptions
or to-the-eyes d3 recasts disagree with Tibetan omission; phrase depth must not
license a false local relation. Compare full original fields, not just tags.

English omits yod pa, narrows rtogs par/perceives and gang/filled; Tibetan
retains be possible, correctly perceives and filled with. Positive wider HGM
records must be confronted explicitly. English gnyis kar/simultaneously and
final gsum po/three different need local semantic support and possible tighter
boundaries. Its full chu yin min water/not-water d3 preserves both English
mentions as one relation; compare against Tibetan's single word/negative pair
and omissions. Both independently allocate the258 technical definition to
phan tshun spangs 'gal; agreement is not sufficient proof. Preserve full
possible/hypothetical/negative causal scope and all source word occurrences.

classes_checked.found: acip: ,AI Dm GU RU RA{tn} MAnd LA Km NI{ry}'A TA YA MI, ,   |   wylie: ai dM gu ru ra maND la kM ni'a ta ya mi,
classes_checked.expected: The Wylie should carry the braced Sanskrit stacks the ACIP encodes: "ratna" (from RA{tn}) and "nirya" (from NI{ry}). Cf. the same mantra at TCS07:82, which is intact: "ai daM gu ru ratna maNDa la kaM niryA ta yA mi".
classes_checked.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes_checked.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). Scored MEDIUM here only because C01:6's own English line supplies the correct reading inches away. The fix belongs in the ACIP-to-Wylie conversion, not in the source text. The trailing "COVERAGE GATE: C01 474->477; 19 open" in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no erratum.

classes_checked.evidence: Verified in build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db, row id=867. C03:303 stores wylie='the preliminaries' (17 chars, confirmed with length(wylie)) and english='I. Why the Steps?' (17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.

classes_checked.found: acip: ,AI Dm GU RU RA{tn} MAnd LA Km NI{ry}'A TA YA MI, ,   |   wylie: ai dM gu ru ra maND la kM ni'a ta ya mi,
classes_checked.expected: The Wylie should carry the braced Sanskrit stacks the ACIP encodes: "ratna" (from RA{tn}) and "nirya" (from NI{ry}). Cf. the same mantra at TCS07:82, which is intact: "ai daM gu ru ratna maNDa la kaM niryA ta yA mi".
classes_checked.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes_checked.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). Scored MEDIUM here only because C01:6's own English line supplies the correct reading inches away. The fix belongs in the ACIP-to-Wylie conversion, not in the source text. The trailing "COVERAGE GATE: C01 474->477; 19 open" in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no erratum.

classes_checked.evidence: Verified in build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db, row id=867. C03:303 stores wylie='the preliminaries' (17 chars, confirmed with length(wylie)) and english='I. Why the Steps?' (17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.

classes_checked.evidence: CLASS ENTRY, not a single instance. Printed footnote reference numbers have been flattened into the running English at ingest, fused to the sentence-final period with no separator. Measured across the whole spine: 307 occurrences in 281 segments across 5 courses - C01 161, C03 95, C16 38, TCS13 7, TCS15 6. Counted on the signature 'sentence-final punctuation + 1-3 digits + space + capital', which excludes thousands separators ('25,000'), section labels ('(S1)') and verse citations ('[I.1b]'); two looser patterns were tried first and gave 1,054 and 867 before those contaminants were excluded. Every instance breaks exact-match search on the final word of its sentence.

Census 2026-09-01 on build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db: 186 segments have length(english) = 1500 (DDA 28, C18 15, C12 14, C13 12, C11 11, Sunlight 11, C17 10, C03 9 - including C03:376, 429, 620, the Reading Eight/Nine/Ten note blocks - MB2 8, C16 7, and 25 further courses); 34 segments EXCEED 1,500, so at least one ingest path does not apply the cap and its reach is not uniform. What is lost is not always apparatus: wherever the cap falls inside a translation, the corpus has no English for the rest of the Tibetan and nothing can align it. The 186 are a floor for the affected rows (a row cut at exactly the cap is certain; a row that happened to be shorter is unaffected).

The cap lives in the canonical ingest (engines/hgm_tools.py), so removing it changes the spine itself and must be re-proved against the full batteries (inviolable rule 2) before any layer is rebuilt on it; the C03:376/429/620 note blocks and any truncated translation would need re-scanning afterwards. classes_checked.expected: The Wylie should carry the braced Sanskrit stacks the ACIP encodes: "ratna" (from RA{tn}) and "nirya" (from NI{ry}). Cf. the same mantra at TCS07:82, which is intact: "ai daM gu ru ratna maNDa la kaM niryA ta yA mi".
classes_checked.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes_checked.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). Scored MEDIUM here only because C01:6's own English line supplies the correct reading inches away. The fix belongs in the ACIP-to-Wylie conversion, not in the source text. The trailing "COVERAGE GATE: C01 474->477; 19 open" in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no erratum.

classes_checked.evidence: Verified in build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db, row id=867. C03:303 stores wylie='the preliminaries' (17 chars, confirmed with length(wylie)) and english='I. Why the Steps?' (17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.

source_row.acip: DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN NAM, 'GA' ZHIG TSAD MA YIN PA DAG LAS GANG YIN, DANG PO LTAR NA BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE RNAG KHRAG LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GSUM GA YIN PA DANG , 'GAL BA LA MA 'KHRUL BA'I TSAD MA YOD PA DANG , PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHU YIN PA DANG CHU MA YIN PA GNYIS KAR TSAD MAS RTOGS PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
source_row.wylie: de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin nam, 'ga' zhig tshad ma yin pa dag las gang yin, dang po ltar na brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de rnag khrag la sogs pa'i dngos po gsum ga yin pa dang , 'gal ba la ma 'khrul ba'i tshad ma yod pa dang , phor pa gang po de chu yin pa dang chu ma yin pa gnyis kar tshad mas rtogs par thal, de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin pa'i phyir
source_row.english: We ask you then a question: in the situation you've just described, is it that the visual consciousness of all three beings are a valid perception, or is it that only one or two of them are a valid perception? Suppose you say all three are valid. Well then, the glass of wet and flowing water must be full of something that is all three different things: pus and blood, and each of the others. And then too it must be possible for there to be multiple and yet still valid perceptions which see one thing in two completely incompatible ways. And finally there must be such a thing as a valid perception which correctly perceives that the glass is filled with something which is simultaneously water and yet not water. Why so? Because, according to your view, the three differing cases of visual consciousness possessed by the three different beings would all have to be valid perception.

classes_checked.expected: The Wylie should carry the braced Sanskrit stacks the ACIP encodes: "ratna" (from RA{tn}) and "nirya" (from NI{ry}). Cf. the same mantra at TCS07:82, which is intact: "ai daM gu ru ratna maNDa la kaM niryA ta yA mi".
classes_checked.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes_checked.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). Scored MEDIUM here only because C01:6's own English line supplies the correct reading inches away. The fix belongs in the ACIP-to-Wylie conversion, not in the source text. The trailing "COVERAGE GATE: C01 474->477; 19 open" in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no erratum.

classes_checked.evidence: Verified in build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db, row id=867. C03:303 stores wylie='the preliminaries' (17 chars, confirmed with length(wylie)) and english='I. Why the Steps?' (17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.

source_row.acip: DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN NAM, 'GA' ZHIG TSAD MA YIN PA DAG LAS GANG YIN, DANG PO LTAR NA BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE RNAG KHRAG LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GSUM GA YIN PA DANG , 'GAL BA LA MA 'KHRUL BA'I TSAD MA YOD PA DANG , PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHU YIN PA DANG CHU MA YIN PA GNYIS KAR TSAD MAS RTOGS PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
source_row.wylie: de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin nam, 'ga' zhig tshad ma yin pa dag las gang yin, dang po ltar na brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de rnag khrag la sogs pa'i dngos po gsum ga yin pa dang , 'gal ba la ma 'khrul ba'i tshad ma yod pa dang , phor pa gang po de chu yin pa dang chu ma yin pa gnyis kar tshad mas rtogs par thal, de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin pa'i phyir
source_row.english: We ask you then a question: in the situation you've just described, is it that the visual consciousness of all three beings are a valid perception, or is it that only one or two of them are a valid perception? Suppose you say all three are valid. Well then, the glass of wet and flowing water must be full of something that is all three different things: pus and blood, and each of the others. And then too it must be possible for there to be multiple and yet still valid perceptions which see one thing in two completely incompatible ways. And finally there must be such a thing as a valid perception which correctly perceives that the glass is filled with something which is simultaneously water and yet not water. Why so? Because, according to your view, the three differing cases of visual consciousness possessed by the three different beings would all have to be valid perception.

classes_checked.expected: The Wylie should carry the braced Sanskrit stacks the ACIP encodes: "ratna" (from RA{tn}) and "nirya" (from NI{ry}). Cf. the same mantra at TCS07:82, which is intact: "ai daM gu ru ratna maNDa la kaM niryA ta yA mi".
classes_checked.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes_checked.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). classes_checked.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes_checked.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). Scored MEDIUM here only because C01:6's own English line supplies the correct reading inches away. The fix belongs in the ACIP-to-Wylie conversion, not in the source text. The trailing "COVERAGE GATE: C01 474->477; 19 open" in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no erratum.

classes_checked.evidence: Verified in build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db, row id=867. C03:303 stores wylie='the preliminaries' (17 chars, confirmed with length(wylie)) and english='I. Why the Steps?' (17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.

classes_checked.found: acip: ,AI Dm GU RU RA{tn} MAnd LA Km NI{ry}'A TA YA MI, ,   |   wylie: ai dM gu ru ra maND la kM ni'a ta ya mi,
classes_checked.expected: The Wylie should carry the braced Sanskrit stacks the ACIP encodes: "ratna" (from RA{tn}) and "nirya" (from NI{ry}). Cf. the same mantra at TCS07:82, which is intact: "ai daM gu ru ratna maNDa la kaM niryA ta yA mi".
classes_checked.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes_checked.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). Scored MEDIUM here only because C01:6's own English line supplies the correct reading inches away. The fix belongs in the ACIP-to-Wylie conversion, not in the source text. The trailing "COVERAGE GATE: C01 474->477; 19 open" in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no erratum.

classes_checked.evidence: Verified in build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db, row id=867. C03:303 stores wylie='the preliminaries' (17 chars, confirmed with length(wylie)) and english='I. Why the Steps?' (17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.
